SMTO-EXE-0270 — This workflow can't run on a schedule because it needs a person

GUID: 3082aa97-f1e4-51c2-abcb-585fb58faee9
Slug: recipe-unattended-not-supported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • This workflow has at least one step where a person must answer or confirm something. A schedule runs with nobody watching, so SMTO won't run this workflow that way. None of its steps ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, find the schedule that starts this workflow, and select Pause (or Delete if you no longer need it). Every scheduled run of this workflow is refused the same way, because nobody is there to answer.
  2. To get the work done now, start it yourself while you're at SMTO, for example by asking for it in a New chat. When you're present, SMTO can stop and wait for your answer at the steps that need a person.
  3. When the run shows Waiting for input, read SMTO's question and type your answer in the message box. Those steps only finish with a person's answer, which a schedule can't give.

What success looks like

  • The schedule shows Paused, and the work you started yourself finishes after you answer its questions.

If it still fails

  • If this work must run with nobody present, select Copy error details and send it to the person who built the workflow. Only a version with no steps that need a person can run on a schedule.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Scheduling or a scheduled run was rejected because the recorded workflow contains manual or confirmation steps, so its risk summary marks it unattended_capable=false.

What this means

  • A scheduled recorded workflow contains a mandatory manual/checkpoint step and its computed risk summary marks unattended execution unsupported. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A scheduled recorded workflow contains a mandatory manual/checkpoint step and its computed risk summary marks unattended execution unsupported.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect mandatory manual/checkpoint steps and the computed unattended_capable flag.

How to fix it

  • create_recipe_schedule (recipes/scheduling.py) and revalidate (recipes/validation.py, when context.agent_recipe_scheduled is set) reject recorded_workflow_v1 artifacts whose risk_summary has unattended_capable=false, i.e. any step whose kind is not 'tool'. Pause or delete the schedule and run the work interactively; only a reviewed definition made entirely of tool steps can run unattended. Note the Workflows page only lists saved_request_v1 definitions.
  • Run this workflow interactively so its required human steps can be answered.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The workflow runs interactively, or a deliberately reviewed definition is genuinely capable of unattended execution.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
